c: The dopamine pathway, step by step

This is a map of how one dopamine-releasing nerve cell in the brain makes, stores and releases dopamine, and of what then happens to the dopamine. Each box is a step, a supporting ingredient, a feedback brake or a related pathway. The biology of each step is well established (
). Whether a weak step explains ADHD in any particular person is an open question (
), and the map does not answer it.

Select any box to read about it in the panel below the map. Selecting a box only changes what you are reading. It does not measure, test or change anything, and it cannot tell you whether you have ADHD or which medicine might suit you.
Solid arrow: next step in the sequence
Main line: inside a brain dopamine cell
Step · The starting material, from the blood.

Tyrosine, an amino acid, is the starting material for dopamine. It comes from protein in food, and the body can also make it from another amino acid, phenylalanine, using the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH).
: Tyrosine in the blood is carried into the brain by LAT1.
: The same starting material and enzymes are also used outside the brain.
No established link (GEN-03). Phenylketonuria (PKU), where PAH does not work, is a separate condition.
This map is not diet advice. It does not show that eating more protein or taking tyrosine changes ADHD symptoms.

To reach brain nerve cells, tyrosine has to cross the blood–brain barrier. It uses LAT1 (gene SLC7A5), a carrier for large neutral amino acids, and competes for it with other amino acids of that type, such as phenylalanine.
: Tyrosine inside the brain is the starting material for tyrosine hydroxylase.
: Tyrosine in the blood is carried into the brain by LAT1.
The LAT1 statement comes from the discussion section of a rat and mouse study and describes the transporter's general role.
Biochemical markers for assessment of metabolic control; Functional effect of Phe-free L-amino acid supplements
Step · Rate-limiting step, by tyrosine hydroxylase.
The enzyme tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) converts tyrosine to L-DOPA. It is the rate-limiting step: the slowest, most tightly controlled step in making dopamine and the other catecholamines.
BH4 (tetrahydrobiopterin), oxygen, and iron held in the enzyme.
: Tyrosine hydroxylase's product, L-DOPA, is converted to dopamine by AADC.
: Tyrosine inside the brain is the starting material for tyrosine hydroxylase.
: Tyrosine hydroxylase needs BH4 to work.
: Dopamine and other catecholamines inhibit tyrosine hydroxylase (end-product feedback).
None established (GEN-03). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists TH within 50 kb (GEN-12).
Levodopa, used mainly for Parkinson's disease, supplies L-DOPA directly and so does not depend on this step (GEN-03).
For understanding only; not a treatment guide.
“Rate-limiting” describes how much dopamine is made. How strongly dopamine signals also depends on packaging, release, receptors and clearance.
The enzyme aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC, gene DDC) converts L-DOPA to dopamine.
PLP (pyridoxal phosphate), the active form of vitamin B6.
: Newly made dopamine is loaded into vesicles by VMAT2.
: Dopamine and other catecholamines inhibit tyrosine hydroxylase (end-product feedback).
: Tyrosine hydroxylase's product, L-DOPA, is converted to dopamine by AADC.
None established (GEN-03). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists DDC within 50 kb (GEN-12).
AADC deficiency is a rare inherited condition. It is mentioned to show that this step matters, not as an explanation of ADHD.
Step · Loaded into storage sacs by VMAT2.
VMAT2 (gene SLC18A2) loads dopamine from inside the cell into vesicles, the small sacs that store it ready for release.
A proton gradient across the vesicle wall, built by the vesicle's proton pump.
: Filled vesicles release dopamine when calcium enters the nerve ending.
: In noradrenaline cells, dopamine inside vesicles is converted to noradrenaline by DBH.
: Newly made dopamine is loaded into vesicles by VMAT2.
: VMAT2 uses the proton gradient built by the vesicle's proton pump.
One small platelet study (GEN-03 rates this Tier C). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists SLC18A2 within 50 kb (GEN-12).
Amphetamine inhibits VMAT2, which releases dopamine from vesicle storage. Methylphenidate is reported to redistribute VMAT2.
For understanding only; not a treatment guide.
After release, vesicles are recycled and refilled; that cycle is not drawn as a separate step.
Step · Calcium triggers vesicles to release dopamine.
When an electrical signal reaches the nerve ending, calcium flows in and triggers vesicles to fuse with the cell membrane, releasing dopamine into the gap between cells.
: Released dopamine binds receptors on nearby cells.
: Released dopamine is carried back into the releasing cell, mainly by DAT in the striatum.
: Released dopamine is broken down by MAO and COMT.
: Released dopamine also binds D2 autoreceptors on the releasing cell.
: Filled vesicles release dopamine when calcium enters the nerve ending.
No specific link stated on this site.
Amphetamine can also move dopamine out of the cell by making the transporter DAT run in reverse (see Reuptake).
For understanding only; not a treatment guide.
Release is adjusted moment to moment by the cell's activity and by autoreceptor feedback.
Support (cofactor or energy) · Cofactor for tyrosine hydroxylase.
Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) is a helper molecule (cofactor) that tyrosine hydroxylase needs. BH4 has its own rate-limiting step, made by the enzyme GTP cyclohydrolase I (GCH1).
: Tyrosine hydroxylase needs BH4 to work.
None established. GCH1 conditions are movement disorders (see GEN-06).
A support link, not a step in the sequence.
Support (cofactor or energy) · Cofactor for AADC.
Pyridoxal phosphate (PLP), the active form of vitamin B6, is the cofactor AADC needs to convert L-DOPA to dopamine.
A support link, not a step. This map does not give supplement advice.
Support (cofactor or energy) · Builds the gradient VMAT2 uses.

A pump in the vesicle wall, the vesicular proton ATPase (V-ATPase), uses ATP to push protons into the vesicle, making it acidic and charged inside. Vesicle transporters, including VMAT2, use this gradient to load their transmitter.
: VMAT2 uses the proton gradient built by the vesicle's proton pump.
The pump is not driven directly by the mitochondria's own proton gradient; energy supply matters through ATP (GEN-03).
Support (cofactor or energy) · Powers the proton pump.
ATP is the cell's energy currency. The vesicle's proton pump is an ATPase: it uses ATP to do its work.
This is not a measure of anyone's energy, tiredness or “battery level”.
Step · Dopamine binds receptors on nearby cells.
Released dopamine binds dopamine receptors on nearby cells. There are five types, D1 to D5, grouped as D1-like (D1 and D5) and D2-like (D2, D3 and D4).
: Released dopamine binds receptors on nearby cells.

Older candidate-gene studies reported signals for DRD4 and DRD5, with heterogeneity, before genome-wide studies (GEN-03). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists DRD4 or DRD5 within 50 kb.
Some medicines act directly on dopamine receptors, such as drugs for Parkinson's disease and antipsychotics.
For understanding only; not a treatment guide.
Receptor signalling inside the receiving cell is not drawn.

Step · DAT carries dopamine back into the cell.

After release, the dopamine transporter (DAT, gene SLC6A3) carries dopamine back into the releasing cell. In the striatum this is the main way released dopamine is cleared. In the frontal cortex DAT is sparse: mouse studies found that dopamine there is taken up mainly by the noradrenaline transporter (NET, gene SLC6A2).
: Released dopamine is carried back into the releasing cell, mainly by DAT in the striatum.
Candidate-gene signal for DAT1 (SLC6A3), with heterogeneity (GEN-03). None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists SLC6A3 within 50 kb (GEN-12).
Methylphenidate inhibits DAT and NET. Amphetamine also inhibits these transporters and can make DAT run in reverse, moving dopamine out of the cell.
For understanding only; not a treatment guide.

The frontal-cortex finding comes from mouse studies; how closely it applies to people is less certain. How much dopamine taken back up is reused is not drawn, because it was not separately source-checked.
Step · MAO and COMT break dopamine down.
Dopamine is broken down by two enzyme families, monoamine oxidase (MAO) and catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT). In the mouse frontal cortex, COMT accounts for about half of dopamine clearance.
: Released dopamine is broken down by MAO and COMT.
No ADHD link is stated for MAO or COMT on GEN-03. None of the 27 regions in the 2023 genome-wide study lists COMT, MAOA or MAOB within 50 kb.
Amphetamine is reported to inhibit monoamine oxidase activity.
For understanding only; not a treatment guide.
The regional figure comes from a mouse study.
Feedback · A brake on the releasing cell.

Some released dopamine binds D2-type autoreceptors on the releasing cell itself. They act as a brake: feedback that controls the cell's firing and how much dopamine it makes, releases and takes back up.
: Released dopamine also binds D2 autoreceptors on the releasing cell.
No specific link stated on this site.
Feedback keeps the system within a working range. It is not a fixed personal set-point.
Related pathway (context) · One extra step in noradrenaline cells.

In noradrenaline-releasing nerve cells there is one extra step. Inside vesicles, the enzyme dopamine β-hydroxylase (DBH) converts dopamine to noradrenaline. This happens in the brain, in nerves elsewhere in the body, and in the adrenal gland.
: In noradrenaline cells, dopamine inside vesicles is converted to noradrenaline by DBH.
ADHD stimulant medicines act on the noradrenaline transporter (NET) as well as DAT.
Methylphenidate and amphetamine both inhibit NET.
For understanding only; not a treatment guide.
Shown for context. This page does not map the noradrenaline system in detail. DBH's own cofactors are not listed because they were not source-checked for this page.
Related pathway (context) · The same enzymes work elsewhere.

Tyrosine hydroxylase also works outside the brain, for example in the adrenal gland, which makes adrenaline. Levodopa taken as a medicine is mostly broken down in the body before it reaches the brain, mainly by AADC, so it is given with a peripheral AADC inhibitor such as carbidopa or benserazide.
: The same starting material and enzymes are also used outside the brain.
Not an ADHD finding; shown so that the brain line is not read as a universal rule.
Carbidopa and benserazide block AADC outside the brain so that more levodopa reaches it.
For understanding only; not a treatment guide.
“Entry into the brain, then conversion” is the order for brain dopamine cells only, not for the adrenal gland or other nerves.
What genetic studies do and do not show here
None of the genes on this map is listed within 50 kb of any of the 27 regions reported by the 2023 genome-wide study (
). Older candidate-gene studies reported signals for DAT1, DRD4 and DRD5, with heterogeneity between studies (
). An association with a region of DNA is not the same as a candidate gene, and neither is a proven causal mechanism (

Methylphenidate mainly inhibits the dopamine and noradrenaline transporters. Amphetamine also inhibits them, can make them run in reverse, and inhibits VMAT2. These notes explain why the medicines are discussed with this pathway. They are not a guide to choosing or changing treatment, which is a decision for a prescriber.
Limits and what is left out
The map is a teaching model of one cell type. Real signalling varies between brain regions and from moment to moment.
Region-specific clearance figures come from mouse studies.
No part of the map describes any individual's biology, levels or treatment.
No checked source stated it explicitly. Add when a source is located and quoted.
